$$

while $\chi ^ { W }$ does not belong to $L$ , implying that not all $\chi ^ { W _ { j } }$ belong to $L$ , and so some $W _ { j }$ does not belong to $\zeta _ { 1 }$ . So $W _ { j }$ can be added to $\zeta _ { 1 }$ , and we can iterate. I

From an optimum common base vector $x$ , an optimum ‘dual solution’ $w _ { 1 } , w _ { 2 }$ can be derived, with a method of Cunningham and Frank [1985]. This gives:

Corollary 47.4a. Problem (47.25) is solvable in strongly polynomial time.

Proof. By Theorem 47.4, we can find a common base vector $x$ of $f _ { 1 }$ and $f _ { 2 }$ maximizing $w ^ { 1 } x$ , in strongly polynomial time. Define a directed graph $D = ( S , A )$ as follows.

For $i = 1 , 2$ , let $A _ { i }$ consist of all pairs $( u , v )$ with $u , v \in S$ such that for each $U \subseteq V$ :

We can find $A _ { i }$ in strongly polynomial time, by finding the minimum of $f _ { i } ( U ) - x ( U )$ over subsets $U$ of $S$ with $u \in U$ and $v \not \in U$ (with any strongly polynomial-time submodular function minimization algorithm).

Let $D$ have arc set $A : = A _ { 1 } \cup A _ { 2 } ^ { - 1 }$ (taking two parallel arcs from $u$ to $v$ in case $( u , v ) \in A _ { 1 }$ and $( v , u ) \in A _ { 2 }$ ). Define a length function $\it l$ on $A$ by, for $( u , v ) \in A$ :

$$
l ( u , v ) : = \left. \begin{array} { c c } { { w ( v ) - w ( u ) } } & { { \mathrm { f o r } \ ( u , v ) \in A _ { 1 } , } } \\ { { 0 } } & { { \mathrm { f o r } \ ( v , u ) \in A _ { 2 } . } } \end{array} \right.
$$

We claim:

$$
D \ { \mathrm { h a s ~ n o ~ n e g a t i v e - l e n g t h ~ d i r e c t e d ~ c i r c u i t s . } }
$$

For suppose that $C$ is a negative-length directed circuit. We take such a $C$ r with $| A C |$ smallest. Then two consecutive arcs in $C$ neither both belong to $A _ { 1 }$ nor both belong to $A _ { 2 } ^ { - 1 }$ . For suppose that $a = ( t , u )$ and $a ^ { \prime } = ( u , v )$ are in $C$ and that they both belong to $A _ { 1 }$ . Then $( t , v ) \in A _ { 1 }$ and $l ( a ) + l ( a ^ { \prime } ) = l ( t , v )$ , contradicting the minimality of $| A C |$ . This similarly gives a contradiction if $a , a ^ { \prime } \in A _ { 2 } ^ { - 1 }$ .

So we can assume that $C$ traverses the vertices $u _ { 0 } , u _ { 1 } , \ldots , u _ { k }$ in this order, with $u _ { 0 } = u _ { k }$ , such that $( u _ { i - 1 } , u _ { i } )$ belongs to $A _ { 1 }$ if $_ i$ is odd, and to $A _ { 2 } ^ { - 1 }$ if $i$ is even. Let $X : = \{ u _ { 1 } , u _ { 3 } , \ldots , u _ { k - 1 } \}$ and $Y : = \{ u _ { 2 } , u _ { 4 } , . . . , u _ { k } \}$ . As $C$ has negative length, we know $l ( A C ) < 0$ , and hence $w ( X ) < w ( Y )$ .

By (47.52), for each $i = 1 , 2$ and for each $U \subseteq V$ with $x ( U ) = f _ { i } ( U )$ we have $| U \cap Y | \geq | U \cap X |$ . Hence there exists an $\varepsilon > 0$ such that the vector

$$
x ^ { \prime } : = x + \varepsilon ( \chi ^ { X } - \chi ^ { Y } )
$$

belongs to $E P _ { f _ { 1 } }$ and to $E P _ { f _ { 2 } }$ . So, since $x ^ { \prime } ( S ) = x ( S )$ , $x ^ { \prime }$ is again a common base vector of $f _ { 1 }$ and $f _ { 2 }$ . However, $w ^ { \mathsf { T } } x ^ { \prime } = w ^ { \mathsf { T } } x + w ( X ) - w ( Y ) > w ^ { \mathsf { T } } x$ , contradicting the fact that $x$ maximizes $w ^ { 1 } x$ . This proves (47.54).

By Theorem 8.7, we can find a potential $p : S  \mathbb { Z }$ for $D$ with respect to $\it l$ , in strongly polynomial time. Then $p$ satisfies

$$
\begin{array} { r l r } & { p ( v ) - p ( u ) \le w ( v ) - w ( u ) } & { \mathrm { ~ f o r ~ e a c h ~ } ( u , v ) \in A _ { 1 } , } \\ & { p ( v ) - p ( u ) \ge 0 } & { \mathrm { ~ f o r ~ e a c h ~ } ( u , v ) \in A _ { 2 } . } \end{array}
$$

Define $w _ { 1 } : = w - p$ and $w _ { 2 } : = p$ . We show that $w _ { 1 }$ and $w _ { 2 }$ are as required in (47.25).

(47.56) implies that, for each $i = 1 , 2$ ,

$$
{ \mathrm { i f ~ } } ( u , v ) \in A _ { i } { \mathrm { ~ t h e n ~ } } w _ { i } ( v ) \geq w _ { i } ( u )
$$

We show that (47.57) implies that, for each $i = 1 , 2$ , $x$ is a base vector of $f _ { i }$ maximizing $w _ { i } ^ { \mathsf { T } } x$ , as required. We may assume $i = 1$ .

Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be the minimum and maximum value (respectively) of the entries in $w _ { 1 }$ . For $j \in \mathbb Z$ , let $U _ { j } : = \{ v \in S \mid w _ { 1 } ( v ) \geq \mu + j \}$ . Then, taking k := ν − µ,

$$

Moreover,

x ( U _ { j } ) = f _ { 1 } ( U _ { j } ) { \mathrm { ~ f o r ~ e a c h ~ } } j = 1 , \ldots , k .

Indeed, for all $s \in U _ { j }$ and $t \in S \setminus U _ { j }$ we have $( s , t ) \notin A _ { 1 }$ (by (47.57), since $w _ { 1 } ( t ) < \mu + j \leq w _ { 1 } ( s ) )$ . Hence, by definition of $A _ { 1 }$ , there is a set $T _ { s , t }$ with $s \in T _ { s , t }$ , $t \notin T _ { s , t }$ , and $x ( T _ { s , t } ) = f _ { 1 } ( T _ { s , t } )$ . Then for any base vector $x ^ { \prime }$ of $f _ { 1 }$ we have

$$

By (47.59), we here have equality throughout for $x ^ { \prime } : = x$ , which proves that $x$ maximizes $w _ { 1 } ^ { 1 } x$ over all base vectors of $f _ { 1 }$ . I

Theorem 47.4 implies for (nonextended) polymatroids (extending a result of Sch¨onsleben [1980] for integer $f _ { 1 }$ and $f _ { 2 }$ for which there is a fixed $K$ with $P _ { f _ { 1 } } \cap P _ { f _ { 2 } } \subseteq [ 0 , K ] ^ { S } .$ ):

Corollary 47.4b. Given submodular set functions $f _ { 1 } , f _ { 2 }$ on $S$ (by value giving oracles) and a weight function $w \in \mathbb { Q } ^ { S }$ , we can find a maximum-weight vector $x \in P _ { f _ { 1 } } \cap P _ { f _ { 2 } }$ in strongly polynomial time.

Proof. We can assume that $f _ { 1 } ( \emptyset ) \ = \ f _ { 2 } ( \emptyset ) = 0$ and that $f _ { 1 }$ and $f _ { 2 }$ are nondecreasing (as we can replace $f _ { i } ( U )$ by $\operatorname* { m i n } _ { T \supseteq U } f _ { i } ( T ) )$ . Extend $S$ with a new element $t$ to a set $S ^ { \prime } : = S + t$ . Define set functions $f _ { 1 } ^ { \prime }$ and $f _ { 2 } ^ { \prime }$ on $S ^ { \prime }$ by:

$$
f _ { i } ^ { \prime } ( U ) : = f _ { i } ( U ) { \mathrm { ~ a n d ~ } } f _ { i } ^ { \prime } ( U + t ) : = 0
$$

for $U \subseteq S$ and $i = 1 , 2$ . Then $f _ { 1 } ^ { \prime }$ and $f _ { 2 } ^ { \prime }$ are submodular (using the nondecreasingness of $f _ { 1 }$ and $f _ { 2 }$ ). Moreover, consider any $\boldsymbol { x } ^ { \prime } \in \mathbb { R } ^ { S ^ { \prime } }$ with $x ^ { \prime } ( S ^ { \prime } ) = 0$ . Let $x$ be the restriction of $x ^ { \prime }$ to $S$ . Then:

$$
x ^ { \prime } \in E P _ { f _ { i } ^ { \prime } } { \mathrm { ~ i f ~ a n d ~ o n l y ~ i f ~ } } x \in P _ { f _ { i } } .
$$

Indeed, if $ { \boldsymbol { x } } ^ { \prime } \in E P _ { f _ { i } ^ { \prime } }$ , then $x ^ { \prime } ( s ) \geq 0$ for each $s \in S$ , since $x ^ { \prime } ( S ^ { \prime } - s ) \ \leq$ $f ^ { \prime } ( S ^ { \prime } - s ) = 0$ and $\overset { \triangledown } { \boldsymbol { x } ^ { \prime } } ( \boldsymbol { S } ^ { \prime } ) = 0$ , implying that $x ( s ) = x ^ { \prime } ( s ) \geq 0$ . Moreover, for each $U \subseteq S$ one has $x ( U ) = x ^ { \prime } ( U ) \leq f _ { i } ^ { \prime } ( U ) = f _ { i } ( U )$ . So $x \in P _ { f _ { i } }$ .

Conversely, if $x \in P _ { f }$ , then for each $U \subseteq S$ one has $x ^ { \prime } ( U ) = x ( U ) \leq$ $f _ { i } ( U ) = f _ { i } ^ { \prime } ( U )$ and $x ^ { \prime } ( U + t ) = x ( U ) - x ( S ) = - x ( S \setminus U ) \leq 0 = f _ { i } ^ { \prime } ( U + t )$ . So $x ^ { \prime } \in E P _ { f _ { i } ^ { \prime } }$ . This proves (47.62).

Define $w ^ { \prime } \in \mathbb { Q } ^ { S ^ { \prime } }$ by $w ^ { \prime } ( v ) : = w ( v )$ if $v \in S$ , and $w ^ { \prime } ( t ) : = 0$ . By Theorem 47.4, we can find a common base vector $x ^ { \prime }$ of $f _ { 1 } ^ { \prime }$ and $f _ { 2 } ^ { \prime }$ maximizing $w ^ { \prime } ^ { 1 } x ^ { \prime }$ in strongly polynomial time. Let $x$ be the restriction of $x ^ { \prime }$ to $S$ . By (47.62), $x$ maximizes $w ^ { 1 } x$ over $P _ { f _ { 1 } } \cap P _ { f _ { 2 } }$ . I

Similarly for maximum-weight common base vectors in (nonextended) polymatroids:

Corollary 47.4c. Given submodular set functions $f _ { 1 } , f _ { 2 }$ on $S$ (by value giving oracles) and a weight function $w \in \mathbb { Q } ^ { S }$ , we can find a maximum-weight common base vector $x$ of $P _ { f _ { 1 } }$ and $P _ { f _ { 2 } }$ in strongly polynomial time.

Proof. Again, we can assume that $f _ { 1 } ( \emptyset ) = f _ { 2 } ( \emptyset ) = 0$ and that $f _ { 1 }$ and $f _ { 2 }$ are nondecreasing. Then the present corollary follows directly from Theorem 47.4, since

$$
P _ { f _ { 1 } } \cap P _ { f _ { 2 } } \cap \{ x \mid x ( S ) = f _ { 1 } ( S ) \} = E P _ { f _ { 1 } } \cap E P _ { f _ { 2 } } \cap \{ x \mid x ( S ) = f _ { 1 } ( S ) \} .
$$

Indeed, if $x \in E P _ { f _ { i } }$ and $x ( S ) = f _ { i } ( S )$ , then $x \ge 0$ , since for any $s \in S$ one has $x _ { s } = x ( S ) - x ( S - s ) \geq f _ { i } ( S ) - f _ { i } ( S - s ) \geq 0$ .

Back to extended polymatroids, Corollary 47.4b yields that we can optimize over the intersection of two extended polymatroids in strongly polynomial time:

Corollary 47.4d. Given submodular set functions $f _ { 1 } , f _ { 2 }$ on $S$ (by value giving oracles) and a weight function $w \in \mathbb { Q } _ { + } ^ { S }$ , we can find a maximum-weight vector $x \in E P _ { f _ { 1 } } \cap E P _ { f _ { 2 } }$ in strongly polynomial time.

Proof. We may assume that $f _ { 1 } ( \varnothing ) = f _ { 2 } ( \varnothing ) = 0$ . Let

$$
L : = \operatorname* { m a x } _ { i = 1 , 2 } ( | f _ { i } ( S ) | + \sum _ { s \in S } | f _ { i } ( \{ s \} ) | ) .
$$

Then $| f _ { i } ( U ) | \leq L$ for each $i = 1 , 2$ and $U \subseteq S$ , since

$$
f _ { i } ( U ) \leq \sum _ { s \in U } f _ { i } ( \{ s \} ) \leq L
$$

and

$$
f _ { i } ( U ) \ge f _ { i } ( S ) - f _ { i } ( S \setminus U ) \ge f _ { i } ( S ) - \sum _ { s \in S \setminus U } f _ { i } ( \{ s \} ) \ge - L .
$$

Let $K : = | S | \cdot L + 1$ . Then for any vertex $x$ of $E P _ { f _ { 1 } } \cap E P _ { f _ { 2 } }$ and any $s \in S$ :

$$
x ( s ) > - K ,
$$

since $x = A ^ { - 1 } b$ for some totally unimodular matrix $A$ and some vector $b$ whose entries are values of $f _ { 1 }$ and $f _ { 2 }$ (as in the proof of Theorem 46.1; observe that the entries of $A ^ { - 1 }$ belong to $\{ 0 , \pm 1 \}$ ).

Define $f _ { i } ^ { \prime } ( U ) : = f _ { i } ( U ) + K \cdot | U |$ . Then

$$
E P _ { f _ { i } ^ { \prime } } = K \cdot { \bf 1 } + E P _ { f _ { i } }
$$

for $i = 1 , 2$ . Hence, by (47.67), all vertices of $E P _ { f _ { 1 } ^ { \prime } } \cap E P _ { f _ { 2 } ^ { \prime } }$ are nonnegative. So any vector $x$ maximizing $w ^ { 1 } x$ over $P _ { f _ { 1 } ^ { \prime } } \cap P _ { f _ { 2 } ^ { \prime } }$ also maximizes $w ^ { 1 } x$ over $E P _ { f _ { 1 } ^ { \prime } } \cap E P _ { f _ { 2 } ^ { \prime } }$ . By Corollary 47.4b, $x$ can be found in strongly polynomial time. I

# 47.5. Contrapolymatroids

Similar results hold for intersections of contrapolymatroids, by reduction to polymatroids. Given supermodular set functions $g _ { 1 }$ and $g _ { 2 }$ on $S$ (by value giving oracles) and a weight function $w \in \mathbb { Q } ^ { S }$ , we can find in strongly polynomial time:

(47.69) (i) a minimum-weight vector in $E Q _ { g _ { 1 } } \cap E Q _ { g _ { 2 } }$ , (ii) a minimum-weight common base vector of $E Q _ { g _ { 1 } }$ and $E Q _ { g _ { 2 } }$ , (iii) a minimum-weight vector in $Q _ { g _ { 1 } } \cap Q _ { g _ { 2 } }$ , and (iv) a minimum-weight common base vector of $Q _ { g _ { 1 } }$ and $Q _ { g _ { 2 } }$ .

Here (i) and (ii) follow from Corollary 47.4d and Theorem 47.4 applied to the submodular functions $- g _ { 1 }$ and $- g _ { 2 }$ . Moreover, (iii) and (iv) follow by application of (i) and (ii) to the supermodular functions $g _ { i }$ given by $\bar { g } _ { i } ( U ) =$ $\operatorname* { m a x } _ { T \subseteq U } g _ { i } ( T )$ for $U \subseteq S$ and $i = 1 , 2$ (assuming without loss of generality $g _ { 1 } ( \emptyset ) = g _ { 2 } ( \emptyset ) = 0$ ).

# 47.6. Intersecting a polymatroid and a contrapolymatroid

Let $f$ be a submodular, and $g$ a supermodular, set function on $S$ . The results on polymatroid intersection also imply that

7.70) a maximum-weight vector in the intersection of the extended polymatroid $E P _ { f }$ and the extended contrapolymatroid $E Q _ { g }$ can be found in strongly polynomial time,

assuming that we have value giving oracles for $f$ and $g$

To see this, we can assume that $f ( \varnothing ) = g ( \varnothing ) = 0$ and $g ( S ) \leq f ( S )$ . Let $t$ be a new element. Define submodular set functions $f _ { 1 }$ and $f _ { 2 }$ on $S + t$ by:

$$
\begin{array} { r l } & { f _ { 1 } ( U ) : = f ( U ) , f _ { 1 } ( U + t ) : = f ( U ) - g ( S ) , f _ { 2 } ( U ) : = f ( S ) - g ( S \backslash U ) , } \\ & { f _ { 2 } ( U + t ) : = - g ( S \backslash U ) , } \end{array}
$$

for $U \subseteq S$ . Reset $f _ { 1 } ( S + t ) : = 0$ . Then for each $x \in \mathbb { R } ^ { S }$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb R$ :

To see necessity, let $( x , \lambda )$ be a common base vector of $E P _ { f _ { 1 } }$ and $E P _ { f _ { 2 } }$ . As $f _ { 1 } ( S + t ) = 0$ , we have $\lambda = - x ( S )$ . Moreover, for any $U \subseteq S$ , we have

$$
\begin{array} { r l } & { x ( U ) \leq f _ { 1 } ( U ) = f ( U ) \mathrm { ~ a n d ~ } } \\ & { x ( U ) = x ( S ) - x ( S \backslash U ) = - \lambda - x ( S \backslash U ) \geq - f _ { 2 } ( ( S \backslash U ) + t ) = g ( U ) . } \end{array}
$$

So $x \in E P _ { f } \cap E Q _ { g }$

To see sufficiency, assume $\lambda = - x ( S )$ and $x \in E P _ { f } \cap E Q _ { g }$ . Then for each $U \subseteq S$ we have:

$$
\begin{array} { r l } & { x ( U ) \leq f ( U ) = f _ { 1 } ( U ) , } \\ & { x ( U + t ) = x ( U ) + \lambda = x ( U ) - x ( S ) \leq f ( U ) - g ( S ) = f _ { 1 } ( U + t ) , } \\ & { x ( U ) = x ( S ) - x ( S \setminus U ) \leq f ( S ) - g ( S \setminus U ) = f _ { 2 } ( U ) , } \\ & { x ( U + t ) = x ( U ) + \lambda = x ( U ) - x ( S ) = - x ( S \setminus U ) \leq - g ( S \setminus U ) } \\ & { = f _ { 2 } ( U + t ) . } \end{array}
$$

So $( x , \lambda )$ is a common base vector of $E P _ { f _ { 1 } }$ and $E P _ { f _ { 2 } }$

This shows (47.72), which implies that finding a minimum-weight vector in $E P _ { f } \cap E Q _ { g }$ amounts to finding a minimum-weight common base vector of $E P _ { f _ { 1 } }$ and $E P _ { f _ { 2 } }$ .

Similarly, we can find a modular function $h$ satisfying $g \ \leq \ h \ \leq \ f$ in strongly polynomial time, if $g \leq f$ (Frank’s discrete sandwich theorem (Corollary 46.2b)). To see this, let $f _ { 1 }$ and $f _ { 2 }$ be as above, and find an $( x , \lambda )$ i n $E P _ { f _ { 1 } } \cap E P _ { f _ { 2 } }$ maximizing $x ( S ) + \lambda$ . If $x ( S ) + \lambda \geq 0$ , then $x \in E P _ { f } \cap E Q _ { g }$ , that is $x$ gives a modular function $h$ with $g \leq h \leq f$ .

# 47.6a. Further notes

Polymatroid intersection is a special case of submodular flow, as discussed in Chapter 60. We therefore refer for further algorithmic work to the notes in Section 60.3e.

A preflow-push algorithm for finding a maximum common vector in the intersection of two polymatroids was presented by Fujishige and Zhang [1992].

Tardos, Tovey, and Trick [1986] gave an improved version of Cunningham and Frank’s polynomial-time algorithm for weighted polymatroid intersection. Fujishige [1978a] gave a (non-polynomial-time) algorithm for weighted polymatroid intersection. Optimizing over the intersection of a base polytope and an affine space was considered by Hartvigsen [1996,1998a,2001a].

Frank [1984c] and Fujishige and Iwata [2000] gave surveys.

# Chapter 48

# Dilworth truncation

If a submodular function $f$ has $f ( \varnothing ) < 0$ , the associated extended polymatroid is empty, as the conditions $x ( U ) \leq f ( U )$ for all $U$ include $x ( 0 ) < f ( 0 )$ . However, by ignoring the condition for $U = \emptyset$ , the obtained polyhedron is yet an extended polymatroid, for a different submodular function, denoted by $\hat { f }$ . This function $\hat { f }$ is called the Dilworth truncation of $f$ .

# 48.1. If $f ( \varnothing ) < 0$

Let $f$ be a submodular set function on $S$ . If $f ( \varnothing ) < 0$ , the associated extended polymatroid $E P _ { f }$ is empty. However, by ignoring the empty set, we yet obtain an extended polymatroid. (The interest in this goes back to Dilworth [1944].)

Consider the system

$$
x ( U ) \leq f ( U ) { \mathrm { ~ f o r ~ } } U \in { \mathcal { P } } ( S ) \setminus \{ \emptyset \} .
$$

and the problem dual to maximizing $w ^ { 1 } x$ over (48.1), for $w \in \mathbb { R } _ { + } ^ { S }$ :

$$
\begin{array} { r l } & { \operatorname* { m i n } \{ \displaystyle \sum _ { U \in \mathcal { P } ( S ) \backslash \{ \emptyset \} } { y ( U ) f ( U ) } \mid } \\ &  \qquad y \in \mathbb { R } _ { + } ^ { \mathcal { P } ( S ) \backslash \{ \emptyset \} } , \displaystyle \sum _ { U \in \mathcal { P } ( S ) \backslash \{ \emptyset \} } { y ( U ) \chi ^ { U } = w \} . } \end{array}
$$

Recall that a collection $\mathcal { F }$ of sets is called laminar if

Then a basic result of Edmonds [1970b] is:

Theorem 48.1. If $f$ is a submodular set function on $S$ , then (48.2) has an optimum solution $y$ with ${ \mathcal { F } } : = \{ U \in { \mathcal { P } } ( S ) \setminus \{ \emptyset \} \mid y ( U ) > 0 \}$ laminar.

Proof. Let $y : { \mathcal { P } } ( S ) \setminus \{ \emptyset \} \to \mathbb { R } _ { + }$ achieve this minimum, with

$$
\sum _ { U \in { \mathcal { P } } ( S ) \setminus \{ \emptyset \} } y ( U ) | U | | S \setminus U |
$$

as small as possible. Assume that $\mathcal { F }$ is not laminar, and choose $T , U \in { \mathcal { F } }$ violating (48.3). Let $\alpha : = \operatorname* { m i n } \{ y ( T ) , y ( U ) \}$ . Decrease $y ( T )$ and $y ( U )$ by $\alpha$ , and increase $y ( T \cap U )$ and $y ( T \cup U )$ by $\alpha$ . Since

$$
\boldsymbol { \chi } ^ { T \cap U } + \boldsymbol { \chi } ^ { T \cup U } = \boldsymbol { \chi } ^ { T } + \boldsymbol { \chi } ^ { U } ,
$$

$y$ remains a feasible solution of (48.2). As moreover

$$
f ( T \cap U ) + f ( T \cup U ) \leq f ( T ) + f ( U ) ,
$$

This implies that system (48.1) is TDI. More generally, it implies the box-total dual integrality of (48.1):

Corollary 48.1a. For any submodular set function $f$ on $S$ , system (48.1) is box-totally dual integral.

Proof. Consider some $w : S \to \mathbb { Z } _ { + }$ , and problem (48.2) dual to maximizing $w ^ { 1 } x$ over (48.1). By Theorem 48.1, this minimum is attained by a $y$ with $\mathcal { F } : =$ $\{ U \in { \mathcal { P } } ( S ) \backslash \{ \emptyset \} \ | \ y ( U ) > 0 \}$ laminar. Hence the constraints corresponding to positive entries in $y$ form a totally unimodular matrix (by Theorem 41.11). Therefore, by Theorem 5.35, (48.1) is box-TDI. I

Let $E P _ { f } ^ { \prime }$ denote the solution set of (48.1). So $E P _ { f } ^ { \prime }$ is nonempty for each submodular function $f$ . As for integrality we have:

Corollary 48.1b. If $f$ is submodular and integer, then $E P _ { f } ^ { \prime }$ is integer.

Proof. Directly from Corollary 48.1a.

In fact, as we shall see in Section 48.2, $E P _ { f } ^ { \prime }$ is again an extended polymatroid.

# 48.2. Dilworth truncation

For each submodular function $f$ , there exists a unique largest submodular function $\hat { f }$ with the property that ${ \hat { f } } ( U ) \leq f ( U )$ for each nonempty $U \subseteq S$ , and ${ \hat { f } } ( \varnothing ) = 0$ . This follows from a method of Dilworth [1944].

Let $f$ be a submodular set function on $S$ . The Dilworth truncation $\hat { f }$ : $\mathcal { P } ( S )  \mathbb { R }$ of $f$ is given by:

for $U \subseteq S$ . So ${ \hat { f } } ( \varnothing ) = 0$ (as for $U = \emptyset$ , only $\mathcal { P } = \emptyset$ qualifies in (48.7)). Dunstan [1976] showed:

Theorem 48.2. $\hat { f }$ is submodular.

Proof. Choose $T , U \subseteq S$ , and let $\mathcal { P }$ and $\mathcal { Q }$ be partitions of $T$ and $U$ (respectively) into nonempty sets with

$$
{ \hat { f } } ( T ) = \sum _ { P \in { \mathcal { P } } } f ( P ) { \mathrm { ~ a n d ~ } } { \hat { f } } ( U ) = \sum _ { Q \in { \mathcal { Q } } } f ( Q ) .
$$

Consider the family $\mathcal { F }$ made by $\mathcal { P }$ and $\mathcal { Q }$ (taking a set twice if it occurs in both partitions). We can transform $\mathcal { F }$ iteratively into a laminar family, by replacing any $X , Y \in { \mathcal { F } }$ with $X \cap Y \neq \emptyset$ and $X \not \subseteq Y \not \subseteq X$ by $X \cap Y , X \cup Y$ . In each iteration, the sum

$$
\sum _ { Z \in { \mathcal { F } } } f ( Z )
$$

does not increase (as $f$ is submodular). As at each iteration the sum

$$
\sum _ { Z \in { \mathcal { F } } } | Z | | S \setminus Z |
$$

decreases (by Theorem 2.1), this process terminates. We end up with a laminar family $\mathcal { F }$ .

The inclusionwise maximal sets in $\mathcal { F }$ form a partition $\mathcal { R }$ of $T \cup U$ , and the remaining sets form a partition $\boldsymbol { S }$ of $T \cap U$ . Therefore,

$$
\begin{array} { r l } & { \hat { f } ( T \cup U ) + \hat { f } ( T \cap U ) \le \displaystyle \sum _ { X \in { \mathcal R } } f ( X ) + \sum _ { Y \in { \mathcal S } } f ( Y ) } \\ & { \le \displaystyle \sum _ { P \in { \mathcal P } } f ( P ) + \sum _ { Q \in { \mathcal Q } } f ( Q ) = \hat { f } ( T ) + \hat { f } ( U ) , } \end{array}
$$

showing that $\hat { f }$ is submodular.

Lov´asz [1983c] observed that $\hat { f }$ is the unique largest among all submodular set functions $g$ on $S$ with $g ( \emptyset ) = 0$ and $g ( U ) \leq f ( U )$ for $U \neq \emptyset$ . Indeed, each subset $U$ of $S$ can be partitioned into nonempty sets $U _ { 1 } , \dots , U _ { t }$ such that

$$
g ( U ) \leq \sum _ { i = 1 } ^ { t } g ( U _ { i } ) \leq \sum _ { i = 1 } ^ { t } f ( U _ { i } ) = \hat { f } ( U )
$$

(the first inequality follows from the submodularity of $g$ , as $g ( \emptyset ) = 0$ ).

Trivially, $E P _ { \hat { f } } = E P _ { f } ^ { \prime }$ . In particular, $E P _ { f } ^ { \prime }$ is an extended polymatroid. Moreover, by (44.34),
